controller_actions.task: Rewrite module.py so solve(data) fully implements the user contract. Raise ValueError if data, base or patch is not a dict. Deep merge patch into base without mutating inputs (deepcopy or build new structures). For each patch key: None value removes the key (no-op if absent); if the key is absent in base, insert the patch value as is (deep copied); if both values are dicts, merge recursively by the same rules; if both are lists, the patch list replaces the base list; otherwise, if the types differ, raise ValueError. Types: dict, list, str, bool, number (int/float but not bool). Booleans and numbers are different types. Null in base with a non-null patch value: types differ, so raise ValueError. If the types are the same scalar (str/str, number/number, bool/bool), the patch value replaces the base value. Key order: base keys in original order, then patch-only keys in patch order. Within nested merges, apply the same rules. Use only the standard library; no I/O.

Write test_cases.json: a JSON list of at least six distinct cases, each with input {base, patch} and exactly one of output or error (exception class name). Expectations must match the user contract. Cover: nested recursive merge; list replacement with no concatenation; null removes an existing key and null for an absent key is a no-op; key order (base keys first, then patch-only keys in patch order); an insert of a new key as is; bool vs number type mismatch -> error ValueError; string vs number mismatch -> error ValueError; non-object base or patch -> error ValueError; null in a nested object removing a nested key.
